en.title: Two-Digit Encryption via Adjacent Sums Modulo Ten
en.description:
Repeatedly build a new array from the sums of adjacent pairs modulo 10 until only two elements remain, then output them as a two-character string; leading 0s must not be dropped.

This site independently wrote the standard I/O and judging; ranges marked as this site's are not original source constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n (2..5000), and the second line contains n digits from 0..9.
en.output: Output a string of exactly two digits, keeping leading 0s.
en.explanation: Example 1: 4 5 6 7→9 1 3→0 4, output 04. Example 2: already two digits, output 00 as is. Example 3: 9 9 9→8 8, output 88.
hints: Compute the adjacent sums layer by layer directly; each layer is one element shorter, and finally concatenate the two digits.
